title: Dalton Caldwell on organizational complexity: how to manage it as a startup grows
summary: Dalton Caldwell argues that complexity is both a cost and a necessity. Large companies need it to ship complex products but it breeds inward-focused politics. Startups should stay simple and focused, then add internal complexity deliberately as traffic and revenue demand it, without overextending.

principles.text: Don't assume success with a simple model will scale up smoothly to more complex real-world conditions.
principles.quote: don’t assume that a successful AI project which utilizes a simple model will seamlessly scale up to more complex circumstances.

principles.text: Large companies need organizational complexity to ship complex products, but it breeds inward-focused politics.
principles.quote: Apple is very complex organization… but that complexity is what allows them to ship very complex products.

principles.text: As companies grow, resources drift toward internal issues rather than customers; don't ship your org chart.
principles.quote: It would seem that the larger a company gets, the more the company tends to allocate resources towards inwardly focused (as opposed to outwardly focused) issues.

principles.text: Focus and simplicity are really complexity management; doing too many things makes the org mirror that mess.
principles.quote: If a company tries to do too many things at once, the company org chart and workflow will naturally begin to model that complexity.

principles.text: Use tools like AWS, outsourced HR and Stripe to keep a startup's internal model simple and easy to change.
principles.quote: Simple models are the easiest to understand and modify on the fly.

principles.text: Add internal complexity deliberately when demand grows (traffic, revenue); refusing to build support or accounting systems in the name of simplicity is a mistake.
principles.quote: A founder probably shouldn’t say: “I believe in simplicity and focus, therefore we will have no systems in place to handle accounting or customer support.”
